rationale: Twenty-two older volunteers consumed a multijuice dessert containing raspberry; outcomes were biochemical oxidative markers, not a measured anxiety comparison. Mixed concentrate is not a frozen raspberry exposure.

Interim report in ten Barrett esophagus patients given freeze-dried black raspberry measured urinary oxidative markers, not anxiety. The shared six-month protocol and authors suggest a study family with ranks 140 and 156, not independent evidence.

Review attributes possible anxiety indications to other Rubus species and raspberry leaf uses to obstetric or enteric indications; primary references and full review need verification before ruling out relevant species or outcomes.

Twenty Barrett esophagus patients took lyophilized black raspberry for six months; abstract reports metabolite and tissue markers, not an anxiety outcome. Rank 156 describes the same-size and protocol study family.
Conference B34 describes 20 Barrett esophagus patients receiving freeze-dried black raspberry for six months and oxidative/tissue markers, not anxiety; same protocol family as rank 140.
Human raspberry dissertation abstract describes acute and two-week consumption with oxidative biomarkers, not anxiety. Rank 184 points to the same repository object and matching study descriptions.
Duplicate repository thesis record of rank 158 with identical human study descriptions; oxidative stress rather than anxiety outcomes in abstract.

Thirty-two adults in three-way crossover consumed breakfast with 0, 125, or 250 g frozen red raspberry; abstract reports postmeal metabolic and oxidative outcomes, not anxiety. The original complete instrument/body remains a separate possible follow-up.

Twenty healthy adults underwent crossover testing of freeze-dried black raspberry cereal bars versus reference and cranberry bars; abstract outcomes were glycemia, appetite and oxidative measures, not anxiety.

Pregnancy cross-sectional survey Table 3: raspberry leaf tea use 76/172 among women reporting aggregate mental symptoms versus 74/157 without, p=.552. Leaf rather than fruit, not Parkinson, anxiety-specific, randomized or evidence of a causal effect.

Thirty men with climacteric symptoms randomized to unripe black raspberry extract or placebo for 12 weeks. Total Aging Male Symptoms scores did not differ significantly; no anxiety item contrast identified in the original article. Extract and non-Parkinson population differ from frozen raspberry claim.
